searchText: <@!130156954273316865> had a question about the JSON RPC spec: what do we return for `baseFeePerGas` on pre-London blocks? Is the field just not there? The spec seems to show that the block will return a `baseFeePerGas` value in all cases. Is it just 0 pre-London? it appears geth just doesn't return any `baseFeePerGas` pre-london Yeah, I think that's the sensible thing to do: it would also help know if a chain supports 1559 or not. Is this an easy spec to make to the change? should be pretty easy, i take a stab at it today or tomorrow hi all, im looking for an easy way to watch the TX pool using golang. Is there a good library where this can easily be done? Main goal is to watch certain TXs and parse them. I just wrote something for that: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22977 In this client, I would use `SubscribePendingTransactions` func in order to just watch _all_ pending TX's, right? Yes very cool, but why is the CI failing? ``` ethclient/gethclient/gethclient_test.go:184:11: unnecessary conversion (unconvert) if uint64(result.Nonce) != nonce { ^ util.go:46: exit status 1 ``` Our linter is pretty rigorous I don't think this is the channel for that kind of discussion lol That's cool. Hope the PR gets merged soon! Next question -- If I'm sitting here mining ETH on my GPU -- Can I use that as my ETH node? Can I watch the TX pool there? <@&595685821026271242> ^ No, your GPU does not verify the blockchain. It receives work packages from the mining pool which are only hashes of the blocks. So you don't even know which transactions your mining on. You need to setup a geth node to watch the txpool (might be able to run it in `syncmode=light` but I'm not sure about that) I'm trying to decide if I should run my own node (resources required? raspi ok?) or just using CloudFlare's ETH node. Just looked it up, you have access to the txpool in the lightclient. So you can start your node with `syncmode=light` which requires ~10 GB and can be run easily on a raspi Realistically, when do you think your PR will be merged? and a new release cut? does geth just run a js interpreter locally? Don't know if it will be part of the next release as we have a lot of stuff to do with London. Next release is probably due monday, so if it's not in by that it will be in 2-3 weeks. Yes, for the RPC this is cool!

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: The spec seems to show that the block will return a `baseFeePerGas` value in all cases. Is it just 0 pre-London?

excerpts.content: should be pretty easy, i take a stab at it today or tomorrow

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content:
hi all, im looking for an easy way to watch the TX pool using golang. Is there a good library where this can easily be done?
Main goal is to watch certain TXs and parse them.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: I just wrote something for that: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/22977

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content: In this client, I would use `SubscribePendingTransactions` func in order to just watch _all_ pending TX's, right?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yes

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content: very cool, but why is the CI failing?

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content:
```
ethclient/gethclient/gethclient_test.go:184:11: unnecessary conversion (unconvert)
    if uint64(result.Nonce) != nonce {
             ^
util.go:46: exit status 1
```

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content: Next question -- If I'm sitting here mining ETH on my GPU -- Can I use that as my ETH node?

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content: Can I watch the TX pool there?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
No, your GPU does not verify the blockchain. It receives work packages from the mining pool which are only hashes of the blocks.
So you don't even know which transactions your mining on. 
You need to setup a geth node to watch the txpool (might be able to run it in `syncmode=light` but I'm not sure about that)

excerpts.author: yuppie.eth
excerpts.content: I'm trying to decide if I should run my own node (resources required? raspi ok?) or just using CloudFlare's ETH node.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
Just looked it up, you have access to the txpool in the lightclient.
So you can start your node with `syncmode=light` which requires ~10 GB and can be run easily on a raspi
